extracted.intended_audience: contributors to mathlib (Lean theorem prover) preparing documentation and pull requests
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for writing module headers, file-level documentation, docstrings, tactic docs, citations, linting tags, and Markdown/LaTeX formatting for mathlib/Lean files and pull requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: File header comment structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each mathlib file should start with: a header comment with copyright information; the list of imports (one on each line); a module docstring containing general documentation, written using Markdown and LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the recommendations in the style guidelines for copyright information. Imports should be listed one per line. The module docstring lives in the header comment delimited by /-! and -/ and should include the mandatory title (first level header) and a summary of the file's content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Header formatting and delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Headers use atx-style headers (hash signs). The open and close delimiters /-! and -/ should appear on their own lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mandatory title of the file is a first level header followed by a summary. Third-level headers (###) are used for titles inside sectioning comments. Ensure delimiters occupy their own lines when the comment is more than one line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module header section order and required/optional sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The module docstring should contain sections (second level headers) in this order: Main definitions (optional), Main statements (optional), Notation (omit only if no notation introduced), Implementation notes, References, Tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation notes should describe important design decisions or interface features, including use of type classes and simp canonical form for new definitions. Tags should be a list of keywords useful for text search in mathlib.

rubrics_metrics.name: References in module header
rubrics_metrics.description: References should refer to bibtex entries in the mathlib citations file (docs/references.bib).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'Citing other works' section for how to add references and make them become links in online docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of doc strings for definitions and major theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Every definition and major theorem is required to have a doc string. Doc strings on lemmas are also encouraged, particularly if the lemma has mathematical content or might be useful in another file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing docstrings are reported by linters such as docBlame and docBlameThm; use lint tags to run specific linters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doc string delimiters and whitespace rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Doc strings are introduced using /-- and closed by -/ above the definition, with either newlines or single spaces between the markers and the text. Subsequent lines in a doc-string should not be indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the doc string appears immediately above the definition/lemma/theorem. Do not indent subsequent lines. Use the specified delimiters exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doc string content and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Doc strings should convey the mathematical meaning of the definition and are allowed to 'lie slightly' about the actual implementation. If a doc string is a complete sentence, it should end in a period. Named theorems should be bold faced (with two asterisks before and after).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise about the mathematical intent; it's acceptable for the docstring to abstract away implementation details. For named theorems (e.g., mean value theorem) use boldface formatting within the docstring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics should have a docstring that matches the Lean documentation style guide. Key points: be complete and self-contained but brief; the docstring should start with a full sentence that has the tactic as the subject; all different options and forms of the tactic should appear in a bulleted list; the 'Examples:' section, if any, should be a sequence of code blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the example 'rewrite [e] uses the expression e as a rewrite rule on the main goal.' Include all options/forms in bullets and provide runnable example code blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linting for documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the docBlame linter to list definitions without doc strings; docBlameThm lists theorems/lemmas without doc strings; tacticDocs lists tactics without docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To run only docBlame, add '# lint only docBlame' to the end of the file. To run docBlame and docBlameThm: '# lint only docBlame docBlameThm'. To run default linters including docBlame and tacticDocs: add '# lint' to the end of the file. To run default plus docBlameThm: '# lint docBlameThm'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Markdown and LaTeX in docstrings
rubrics_metrics.description: Doc strings can contain Markdown and LaTeX. References to Lean declarations or variables are generally put in backticks. LaTeX can be included inline with $ ... $, in display mode with $$ ... $$, or using environments \begin{*} ... \end{*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer fully-qualified names (e.g. finset.card_pos) to create links in the online docs. Raw URLs should be enclosed in angle brackets <...> to make them clickable. These LaTeX modes correspond to MathJax settings of the online docs; preview in the Lean doc preview or a MathJax sandbox similar to math.stackexchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking and URL formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing the fully-qualified name will turn the name into a link on the online docs. Raw URLs should be enclosed in angle brackets to ensure they are clickable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with URLs containing parentheses or special symbols which may not be parsed correctly by the markdown renderer; use angle brackets to help. Use fully-qualified Lean names to produce links to declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectioning comments usage
rubrics_metrics.description: It's common to structure a file in sections described with module documentation /-! ... -/ at the beginning; sectioning comments often correspond to section or namespace commands but this is not required. Sectioning comments are for display and readability only and have no semantic meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can use sectioning comments inside a section or namespace, and you can have multiple sections or namespaces following one sectioning comment. Use third-level headers (###) for titles inside sectioning comments. When the comment is more than one line, /-! and -/ should appear on their own lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theories documentation vs file docstrings
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to documentation in Lean files, there are theories documentation pages for overviews spanning several Lean files and for more mathematical explanations where formalization requires exotic points of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put broader overviews or multi-file expositions in the theories documentation area (examples include topology documentation). Use file docstrings for file-local summaries and sectioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite other works (bibtex and citation syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: To cite papers and books in doc strings, add the references to docs/references.bib and normalize the file with bibtool using the provided command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization command: bibtool --preserve.key.case=on --preserve.keys=on --print.use.tab=off --pass.comments=on -s -i docs/references.bib -o docs/references.bib. To get clickable links in online docs, use either [key] or [custom text][key]. Note: you currently cannot use the closing square bracket ] symbol in the link text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and spelling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation should be written in English. Any common spelling (British, American or Australian) is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pull requests should not be made that only change which of these spellings are used, but it's acceptable to change spelling as part of a PR that substantially enhances the documentation. Declaration names, however, should use American English spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and canonical examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of files are maintained as examples of good documentation style (e.g., Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.PadicNorm, Mathlib.Topology.Basic, Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Basic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these canonical files for concrete examples of header layout, docstrings, sectioning, and formatting that meet the style guidelines.
